legal_ref: Wet op de omzetbelasting 1968, art. 9 lid 1
quote: Artikel 9 1 De belasting bedraagt 21 percent. 2 In afwijking van het eerste lid bedraagt de belasting: a. 9 percent voor leveringen van goederen en diensten, genoemd in de bij deze wet behorende tabel I; b. nihil voor leveringen van goederen en diensten, genoemd in de bij deze wet behorende tabel II ... — The tax is 21%; by derogation it is 9% for the goods and services in Table I and nil for those in Table II.
source_title: wetten.overheid.nl – Wet op de omzetbelasting 1968, version in force from 01-01-2026 (consulted 07-10-2026); start date from the consolidated versions in force 01-07-2012 (art. 9: 19 percent) and 01-10-2012 (art. 9: 21 percent)

reduced_rates.scope: Table I: foodstuffs and food in restaurants/catering, non-alcoholic drinks, water, medicines and medical aids, books and e-books/news sites, flowers and plants, passenger transport, camping, sports facilities, admission to museums/zoos/concerts/theatre etc., hairdressing, minor repairs (bicycles, shoes, clothing), domestic cleaning, insulation and painting of older dwellings, performing artists
Table II (nil rate): exports, intra-EU supplies and related services, international transport; supply and installation of solar panels on or near dwellings

notes: The standard rate went from 19% to 21% on 1 Oct 2012. The 6% reduced rate became 9% on 1 Jan 2019. In the 2026 text, Table I item b.11 (hotel and other accommodation, 'logies') is marked 'vervallen', so short-stay hotel accommodation appears to be at 21% from 1 Jan 2026 while camping (b.10) stays at 9%. The consolidated text also notes amendments that have no commencement date yet. TEDB (2026-07-01) shows 21% / 9% / 0%, consistent.
unverified: Amending act behind the 1 Oct 2012 increase (Belastingplan / Wet verhoging algemeen btw-tarief 2012) not identified by Staatsblad number; date taken from the consolidated-version boundaries on wetten.overheid.nl
Hotel accommodation moving from 9% to 21% on 2026-01-01 is inferred from Table I item b.11 being repealed, not from the amending act
